scope: one selected development case; timestep sensitivity, not statistical robustness
limits: Finest dt is a numerical reference, not an exact continuous-time solution.
Ranking stability does not establish accuracy of individual service times.
Compute timestamps, transfer completion, ground arbitration and fixed merge delay remain quantized.
Actual link throughput counts transmitted bytes including relay hops, not unique useful payload.
Network nominal capacity counters are not used as visibility-conditioned capacity evidence.
Common-completion latency retains success-subset bias; complete-population age metrics are primary.
Native task_trace_sha256 includes step indices; cross-dt equality uses physical_task_trace_sha256.

posthoc_interpretation.scope: Only validation_near_high_1, 105 fixed task arrivals, four methods and three time steps; not all six conditions.
posthoc_interpretation.native_dt1_crosscheck: All four dt=1 records exactly match corresponding validation baseline task_outcomes, network, and native task_trace_sha256.

cgs_traffic.attribution: Edge totals change materially on multiple source-to-neighbor links; no tile-level transfer log is available. raw_relay_hops does not count ordinary offload paths. Exact task/decision attribution remains unresolved.

posthoc_interpretation.conclusion: Hour-scale age-score stability does not imply second-scale latency or communication-action convergence. The finest time step is only a numerical reference. Orbit/visibility 10s and contact scan 30s were held fixed and were not themselves refined.
